title: finding(types): `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` is a TYPE-LEVEL ratchet judged only by `tsc`, but wears a `.test.ts` extension — a vitest run of a violated tree exits 0
body:
Dedup keywords: `zod-mirror-parity` · type-level · vitest · `tsc` · false-green

Surfaced by the `os-dev` seat verifying objectui#9256 (PR objectui#9544) and **re-derived on disk** by the `domain:ui` execution seat before filing. ⛔ Unassigned and ungraded.

## The reading

`packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` (4519 lines) is a **type-level ratchet**, enforced by `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`. But it is spelled as a `.test.ts`, so the obvious way to "check parity" is to run it with vitest — and that exercises the wrong half.

Measured at `origin/main`:

| probe | reading |
|---|---|
| type-level assertions (never-typed decls / `Expect<` / `Equal<`) | **72** |
| runtime `expect()` calls | **53** |
| `packages/types/tsconfig.test.json:30` | `"include": ["src/**/*.test.ts", …]` ⇒ the file IS in the type-check program |

⇒ the file carries **both** halves. ⭐ That is exactly why the false green is convincing: vitest runs the 53 runtime assertions and reports a real pass, while the 72 that carry the ratchet are invisible to it.

## ⚠️ Measured on a violated tree, in both directions

objectui#9256's verification mutated the mirror (`.omit()`-ing both content keys off it) and ran the file **both ways on the identical tree**:

- `vitest` ⇒ **exit 0** ← the ratchet is violated and this says nothing
- `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` ⇒ **exit 2**, `TS2322`

⭐ The seat that ran it **discarded** the vitest green rather than reporting it as a pass — which is the only reason the mutation leg is worth anything. A run that had stopped at the green would have recorded an ablation that proves nothing, and looked rigorous doing it.

## The defect, stated narrowly

⛔ Not "vitest is wrong" and ⛔ not "the assertions are wrong". It is that **the file does not say which command judges it**, while wearing the extension of the command that does not.

## Options (⛔ not a ruling)

1. **Say so in the file's own header** — one sentence naming `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` as the arbiter and vitest as exercising only the runtime census. Cheapest; the repo already uses this "which gate arbitrates" habit elsewhere.
2. **Add a runtime guard** that fails under vitest unless the type-check has been run — ⚠️ awkward, and invents a second source of truth.
3. **Split the file** — the type-level ratchet into a non-`.test.ts` compiled fixture, the runtime census staying a test. Truest, and the largest change.

## Related

objectui#9256 / PR objectui#9544 — where it was measured. ⚠️ Same class as this repo's standing rule that `exit 2 [unbuilt-package]` is PREREQUISITE NOT MET rather than a pass: a green that answers a different question than the one asked.
